items.title: Delhi's air quality slips into 'severe' category on Diwali; Mumbai's AQI at 170
items.summary: Delhi experienced a significant decline in air quality overnight, with areas recording severe pollution levels. The Central Pollution Control Board reported an Air Quality Index of 406 at ITO, indicating hazardous conditions. Visibility was greatly reduced as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city during the early morning hours. Rajiv Chowk and South Extension also reported very poor air quality readings.

facts.text: Kishan Reddy, will inaugurate three major facilities-International Hostel, Advanced Geophysical Data Processing Laboratory and Digital Studio-at the Geological Survey of India Training Institute (GSITI), Bandlaguda-Nagole, Hyderabad, on 10th November 2026 at 09:30 hrs.

items.title: INAUGURAL INDIA–MYANMAR BILATERAL TRI-SERVICES HADR EXERCISE ‘RAHAT MITRA’ CONCLUDES AT CHENNAI
items.summary: 09 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi The inaugural bilateral Tri-Services Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise ‘RAHAT MITRA’, conducted between the Defence Forces of India and Myanmar on 05 and 06 Nov 2026, concluded at Chennai.

facts.text: The two-day exercise brought together personnel from the Indian Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force, along with a delegation from the Myanmar Defence Forces, to enhance operational interoperability, improve coordination and facilitate the exchange of Best Practices in disaster response operati…
The exercise commenced with a focus on joint planning and familiarisation with HADR capabilities.
The exercise also facilitated familiarisation with each other’s capabilities and procedures, contributing to improved coordination during disaster response operations.

The successful culmination of the inaugural exercise reinforces the commitment of India and Myanmar to advancing bilateral defence cooperation and enhancing collective preparedness for disaster response.

items.title: Wisconsin couple manages 500-acre forest for wildlife, eyes $10,000 award
items.summary: Jesse and Kylie Sebero are managing over 500 acres of forest in Marinette County, Wisconsin. They focus on timber production while ensuring ecological balance and wildlife conservation. The couple also opens their land for educational tours, helping others learn about forest management. They have been nominated for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award for their significant contributions.
